page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0 placing it in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression (34.85 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (15.13 GB/sec) both rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The multi-core Geekbench score of 4968.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 4403.68 fall into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth at 32.55 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 20.39 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 25%.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core and weak memory bandwidth, the c4n-highcpu-4 is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale software compilation, the latter scoring in the bottom 25% on Geekbench. Instead, its strong single-core performance and advanced matrix instruction support make it efficient for single-threaded processing, text processing, and light machine learning inference, as demonstrated by an average prompt processing speed of 637.06 tokens/sec on a 135M LLM model. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense compute profile for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints or local storage.
